arxiv-2104-06084.title: On the Efficiency of Polar-like Decoding for Symmetric Codes
arxiv-2104-06084.creator: Kirill Ivanov, Rüdiger L. Urbanke
arxiv-2104-06084.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kirill Ivanov, Rüdiger L. Urbanke. The recently introduced polar codes constitute a breakthrough in coding theory due to their capacity-achieving property. This goes hand in hand with a quasilinear construction, encoding, and successive cancellation list decoding procedures based on the Plotkin construction.

arxiv-2111-02370.title: The solar corona as an active medium for magnetoacoustic waves
arxiv-2111-02370.creator: D. Y. Kolotkov, D. I. Zavershinskii, V. M. Nakariakov
arxiv-2111-02370.description: Abstract The presence and interplay of continuous cooling and heating processes maintaining the corona of the Sun at the observed one million K temperature were recently understood to have crucial effects on the dynamics and stability of magnetoacoustic waves. These essentially compressive waves perturb the coronal thermal equilibrium, leading to the phenomenon of a wave-induced thermal misbalance.

arxiv-2302-01531.title: Universal multi-stream radial structures of cold dark matter halos
arxiv-2302-01531.creator: Yohsuke Enomoto, Takahiro Nishimichi, Atsushi Taruya
arxiv-2302-01531.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yohsuke Enomoto, Takahiro Nishimichi, Atsushi Taruya. Virialized halos of cold dark matter generically exhibit multi-stream structures of accreted dark matter within an outermost radial caustic known as the splashback radius. By tracking the particle trajectories that accrete onto the halos in cosmological N N -body simulations, we count their number of apocenter passages ( p p ), and use them to characterize the multi-stream structure of dark matter particles.

arxiv-2303-06795.title: Roadmap towards Meta-being
arxiv-2303-06795.creator: Tianyi Huang, Stan Z. Li, Xin Yuan, Shenghui Cheng
arxiv-2303-06795.description: Abstract Metaverse is a perpetual and persistent multi-user environment that merges physical reality with digital virtuality. It is widely considered to be the next revolution of the Internet. Digital humans are a critical part of Metaverse. They are driven by artificial intelligence (AI) and deployed in many applications.

arxiv-2504-09917.title: Creation of chaos for interacting Brownian particles
arxiv-2504-09917.creator: Armand Bernou, Mitia Duerinckx, Matthieu Ménard
arxiv-2504-09917.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Armand Bernou, Mitia Duerinckx, Matthieu Ménard. We consider a system of N N Brownian particles, with or without inertia, interacting in the mean-field regime via a weak, smooth, long-range potential, and starting initially from an arbitrary exchangeable N N -particle distribution.

arxiv-2509-11232.title: MIS-LSTM: Multichannel Image–Sequence LSTM for Sleep Quality and Stress Prediction
arxiv-2509-11232.creator: Seongwan Park, Jieun Woo, Siheon Yang
arxiv-2509-11232.description: Abstract This paper presents MIS-LSTM, a hybrid framework that joins CNN encoders with an LSTM sequence model for sleep quality and stress prediction at the day level from multimodal lifelog data. Continuous sensor streams are first partitioned into N-hour blocks and rendered as multi-channel images, while sparse discrete events are encoded with a dedicated 1D-CNN.

arxiv-2511-14113.title: Coffee: Co ntrollable Di ff usion Fin e -tuning
arxiv-2511-14113.creator: Ziyao Zeng, Jingcheng Ni, Ruyi Liu, Alex Wong
arxiv-2511-14113.description: Abstract Text-to-image diffusion models can generate diverse content with flexible prompts, which makes them well-suited for customization through fine-tuning with a small amount of user-provided data. However, controllable fine-tuning that prevents models from learning undesired concepts present in the fine-tuning data—and from entangling those concepts with user prompts—remains an open challenge.

arxiv-2601-09825.title: Eluder dimension: localise it!
arxiv-2601-09825.creator: Alireza Bakhtiari, Alex Ayoub, Samuel Robertson, David Janz, Csaba Szepesvári
arxiv-2601-09825.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Alireza Bakhtiari, Alex Ayoub, Samuel Robertson, David Janz, Csaba Szepesvári. We establish a lower bound on the eluder dimension of generalised linear model classes, showing that standard eluder dimension-based analysis cannot lead to first-order regret bounds. To address this, we introduce a localisation method for the eluder dimension; our analysis immediately recovers and improves on classic results for Bernoulli bandits, and allows for the first genuine first-order bounds for finite-horizon reinforcement learning tasks with bounded cumulative returns.

pmc-10562079.title: Diathermy and bone sawing are high aerosol yield procedures
pmc-10562079.creator: Victoria Hamilton, Sadiyah Sheikh, Alicja Szczepanska, Nick Maskell, Fergus Hamilton, Jonathan P. Reid, Bryan R. Bzdek, James R. D. Murray
pmc-10562079.description: AimsOrthopaedic surgery uses many varied instruments with high-speed, high-impact, thermal energy and sometimes heavy instruments, all of which potentially result in aerosolization of contaminated blood, tissue, and bone, raising concerns for clinicians’ health. This study quantifies the aerosol exposure by measuring the number and size distribution of the particles reaching the lead surgeon during key orthopaedic operations.

pmc-10718159.title: Emetine dihydrochloride alleviated radiation‐induced lung injury through inhibiting EMT
pmc-10718159.creator: Xin Wang, Mo Li, Jizhong Yin, Jiayan Fang, Yimeng Ying, Tianxia Ye, Fangxiao Zhang, Shumei Ma, Hongran Qin, Xiaodong Liu
pmc-10718159.description: Radiation‐induced lung injury (RILI), divided into early radiation pneumonia (RP) and late radiation‐induced pulmonary fibrosis (RIPF), is a common serious disease after clinical chest radiotherapy or nuclear accident, which seriously threatens the life safety of patients. There has been no effective prevention or treatment strategy till now.

pmc-11310950.title: Challenges of the Calgary–Cambridge Consultation Guide in Veterinary Multicultural and Multilingual Scenarios and the Role of Veterinary Translators
pmc-11310950.creator: Angel Almendros, Paulo V. Steagall, Suen Caesar Lun, Jonathan Speelman, Antonio Giuliano
pmc-11310950.description: Simple SummaryThe success and the satisfaction of clinicians in practice relies heavily on how consultations, communication, and relationships are built with clients. Very knowledgeable and competent veterinarians might not be able to provide their services if the client declines their services based on misperceptions or lack of understanding, potentially resulting in lack of treatments of pets in need.

pmc-11322766.title: The potential linkage between sediment oxygen demand and microbes and its contribution to the dissolved oxygen depletion in the Gan River
pmc-11322766.creator: Shoutao Cheng, Fansheng Meng, Yeyao Wang, Jiasheng Zhang, Lingsong Zhang
pmc-11322766.description: The role of sediment oxygen demand (SOD) in causing dissolved oxygen (DO) depletion is widely acknowledged, with previous studies mainly focusing on chemical and biological SOD separately. However, the relationship between the putative functions of sediment microbes and SOD, and their impact on DO depletion in overlying water, remains unclear.

pmc-11402088.title: Characterizing medication safety incidents in surgical patients: a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of incident reports
pmc-11402088.creator: Noah Sagua, Andrew Carson-Stevens, Kathryn Lynette James
pmc-11402088.description: Background:Medication-related safety incidents (MSIs) are among the most frequent contributors to preventable harm in hospital patients. There is a paucity of research that explores the factors that contribute to MSIs across the departments of high-risk specialties such as surgery.Objectives:To characterize MSIs involving surgical patients across two secondary care sites at a University Health Board.

pmc-13004729.creator: Stefan Stanovcic, Mira Milisavljevic, Natalija Azanjac, Snezana Kojic, Milorad Kojic
pmc-13004729.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This work builds upon our previous “repopulation upon shattering” (RUS) studies in the yeast-like microbe Ustilago maydis, focusing mainly on a deeper understanding of the suicidal type of death caused by self-generated hypoxia (SGH).

pmc-13137359.title: Preoperative Multi-modal Images-based Radiomics Model for Distinguishing Spinal Osteosarcoma and Chondrosarcoma
pmc-13137359.creator: Chenxi Wang, Yuan Yuan, Kai Ye, Zhenyu Li, Huishu Yuan, Ning Lang
pmc-13137359.description: Introduction:This study aimed to develop and validate a radiomics fusion model based on CT and MRI for distinguishing between spinal osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma, and to compare the performance of models derived from different imaging modalities.Methods:A retrospective analysis was conducted on 63 patients with histologically confirmed spinal osteosarcoma (n=20) and chondrosarcoma (n=43).

pmc-13195513.title: Fpr1p mediates the synergistic effect of rapamycin or tacrolimus with caspofungin in Clavispora lusitaniae in vitro
pmc-13195513.creator: Maxime Lefranc, Isabelle Accoceberry, Valérie Fitton-Ouhabi, Nicolas Biteau, Thierry Noël
pmc-13195513.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesCaspofungin is an echinocandin antifungal agent that inhibits glucan synthesis, an essential component of the fungal cell wall. Rapamycin and tacrolimus are immunosuppressant drugs that share the same cellular receptor, the peptidyl-prolyl isomerase Fpr1p. This study investigated the interactions between rapamycin or tacrolimus and caspofungin in inhibiting the growth of wild-type Clavispora lusitaniae and isogenic strains engineered to overexpress or lack the FPR1 gene.MethodsDrug interactions were assessed using the microdilution checkerboard method in liquid medium.

pmc-13297024.title: Volume Alterations in Thalamic Subnuclei in Parkinson's Disease Dementia and Machine Learning‐Based Prediction of Diagnosis and Severity
pmc-13297024.creator: Yingchuan Chen, Guanyu Zhu, Ruoyu Ma, Rujin Wang, Fangang Meng, Anchao Yang, Tingting Du, Jianguo Zhang
pmc-13297024.description: BackgroundCognitive decline in Parkinson's disease (PD) is associated with pathological alterations within the thalamus. Nevertheless, volumetric changes in the specific subnuclei of the thalamus in PD patients with dementia (PD‐D) remain inadequately characterized. Furthermore, the clinical challenges of diagnosing PD‐D at an individual level and forecasting the trajectory of cognitive decline persist.
